findings.proof: For the node A={(f,g) in k[[x]]×k[[y]]:f(0)=g(0)}, the conductor is (x)×(y). Both d=(x³)×(y³) and c=(x)×(y²) lie in it, with d⊂c. In B/d the subspace c/d has basis (x,0),(x²,0),(0,y²). Branch swap is an algebra automorphism of B/d and sends (x,0) to (0,y), which is outside c/d. Thus the unrestricted ideal-invariance assertion is false.

proof: Put B=product_i k[[t_i]] and r=product_i(t_i), so c_N=r^N. Fix N0>=1 such that c_N0 lies in the conductor and hence in A. Then c_N for N>=N0 is cofinal among finite-colength ideals contained in the conductor; it is not cofinal among literally all ideals, such as the zero ideal.

For M>=N>=N0, c_N/c_M is a power of the Jacobson radical of B/c_M, hence characteristic under its k-algebra automorphisms. Reduction gives pi_MN:Aut(B/c_M)→Aut(B/c_N). Branch permutations lift, and a truncated uniformizer a1 t+... with a1 nonzero lifts its coefficients to orderM; pi is surjective. This describes the actual finite algebraic groups here (k is algebraically closed of characteristic0 by the standing2.26 and2.33 assumptions).

Let H_N be the stabilizer of A/c_N in Aut(B/c_N). Because c_N⊂A, the subalgebra A/c_M is exactly the inverse image of A/c_N under B/c_M→B/c_N. Consequently pi_MN^{-1}(H_N)=H_M. In particular ker(pi_MN)⊂H_M, and pi_MN(H_M)=H_N by surjectivity.

These identities yield canonical pointed homogeneous-space isomorphisms Aut(B/c_M)/H_M ≅ Aut(B/c_N)/H_N. They justify independence along this characteristic cofinal system, not the original assertion for arbitrary non-characteristic conductor subideals.
